query: How does incident resolution efficiency vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: primary_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Clean, well-separated categorical (printer, monitor, software, etc.) that is external to resolution efficiency and can be segmented on to compare resolution times across asset classes.

per_column.name: specific_failure_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Interpretable failure-type categories (hardware_malfunction, paper_jam, disk_failure) that are associational to how quickly incidents resolve; some low-count tails but overall meaningful.

per_column.name: issue_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Complexity buckets (requires_replacement vs simple_functional_issue) are interpretable and plausibly drive efficiency, but this borders on restating resolution effort; still segmentable and external enough to be informative.

per_column.name: resolution_scope
per_column.rationale: Describes the nature of the resolution itself (repair_required, equipment_replacement). This is largely a restatement of the resolution outcome rather than an independent explanatory variable, so its correlation with efficiency is somewhat tautological.

per_column.name: issue_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Severity levels (single_failure, critical_system_outage, performance_degradation) are interpretable and classically associated with resolution efficiency; dominant single category but with meaningful contrasting tails.

per_column.name: issue_frequency_pattern
per_column.rationale: Binary isolated vs recurring split is clean, external, and offers a clear comparison axis for efficiency.

per_column.name: assignment_hand_off_evidence
per_column.rationale: Whether assigned and closing person differ is an interpretable operational binary plausibly linked to resolution efficiency (hand-offs add delay); good segmentation variable.

per_column.name: requester_type
per_column.rationale: Standard vs system_integration user is a clean binary segmentation external to the focus; its 390/110 split mirrors the hand-off column exactly, hinting at possible redundancy, but semantically distinct and interpretable.

judge.rationale: As a set, these columns provide multiple interpretable, well-separated categorical segmentations (asset type, failure mechanism, severity, frequency, hand-off, requester type) that a human can group on and compare against resolution efficiency, satisfying the EDA claim. They are associational rather than opaque model scores and avoid pure text-length/token mechanics. Weaknesses: 'resolution_scope' and partly 'issue_complexity_signal' restate the resolution outcome itself, making any correlation with efficiency near-tautological; and the identical 390/110 distribution shared by 'assignment_hand_off_evidence' and 'requester_type' suggests possible redundancy/derivation. Overall a strong, mostly interpretable set with a couple of restatement-leaning columns.
